import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Calculate total spending on all products
spending_cols = [
    'MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts',
    'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds'
]
df['Total_Spending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Drop rows where 'Income' is NaN, as it's crucial for this visualization
df_cleaned = df.dropna(subset=['Income'])

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_cleaned,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    hue='Education',
    palette='viridis',  # A perceptually uniform colormap
    alpha=0.7,          # Transparency for better visibility of overlapping points
    s=70                # Size of the points
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Customer Total Spending vs. Income by Education Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Income', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending on Products', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlap with the plot
plt.legend(title='Education Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Adjust layout to make sure everything fits without overlapping, especially the legend
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1])

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Calculate total spending on all products
spending_cols = [
    'MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts',
    'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds'
]
df['Total_Spending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Drop rows where 'Income' is NaN, as it's crucial for this visualization
df_cleaned = df.dropna(subset=['Income'])

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_cleaned,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    hue='Education',
    palette='viridis',  # A perceptually uniform colormap
    alpha=0.7,          # Transparency for better visibility of overlapping points
    s=70                # Size of the points
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Customer Total Spending vs. Income by Education Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Income', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending on Products', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlap with the plot
plt.legend(title='Education Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Adjust layout to make sure everything fits without overlapping, especially the legend
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1])

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
